stories.title: 30C expected as heat warning issued for most of country
stories.summary: Temperatures could reach up to 30C in parts of Ireland, as a new Status Yellow high temperature warning will come into effect for most of the country later. The warning for Carlow, Kildare, Kilkenny, Laois, Longford, Offaly, Westmeath, Cavan, Donegal, Munster and all of Connacht will come into effect at 12pm and will last until 6am on Friday. Met Éireann said 30C is likely in counties under the high temperature warning. Yesterday, the mercury hit 29.3C at Shannon Airport. It was cooler in Dublin, with temperatures reaching 21.3C at Dublin Airport.

stories.title: US launches fresh Iran strikes, reimposes naval blockade
stories.summary: US forces have carried out strikes against Iran for a fourth day in a row and reimposed a naval blockade to prevent ships from sailing to or from the country's ports. While US President Donald Trump backtracked on his threat to heavily tax ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, he warned he would expand US strikes on Iran next week to target power plants and bridges if Iran does not agree to a deal. "Next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges," Mr Trump said in an interview on Fox News. "We're going to knock out all their power plants. We're going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate," he added.

stories.title: Tusla reports 10% rise in child safety, welfare referrals
stories.summary: Tusla experienced a 10% increase in child safety and welfare referrals last year. It is the first time that the number of referrals to the Child and Family Agency has surpassed 100,000, according to its 2025 annual report, reaching 106,444. A total of 55,483 referrals related to individual children, equating to approximately one in 23 children living in Ireland (Census 2022). Demand remained high across Tusla services throughout the year, including child safety and welfare, educational support, family support, residential care and Special Care and supports for Separated Children Seeking International Protection (SCSIP).

stories.title: 988 garda escorts used on 10 deportation flights
stories.summary: A total of 988 garda escorts accompanied 377 returnees on 10 deportation flights out of Ireland since February last year. New figures show that the cost of the deportation operations totalled €3.9m, or around €10,344 per returnee. The €3.9 million spend does not include the costs of the garda escorts on the flights. In a letter to the Public Accounts Committee, Secretary General at the Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration, Doncha O'Sullivan said: "The rationale for the number of garda escorts on the flight is linked to the risk posed by the passengers."

stories.title: 'Vigilance' urged as hot spell raises gorse fire risks
stories.summary: Fire services are urging people to be "vigilant and cautious" as the hot spell has led to a number of gorse fires around the country. A large fire Co Kerry, which damaged around 15 hectares of land within Killarney National Park, has been extinguished after the alarm was raised at around 5.30pm yesterday. The areas most affected were at Five Mile Bridge on the N71 Killarney-Kenmare road and Moll's Gap. Four fire units from three stations were involved in the operation, with two helicopters on standby.

stories.title: ICE suspends traffic stops in wake fatal shootings
stories.summary: The US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency has ordered its officers to suspend most vehicle stops around the country, after agents fatally shot two men six days apart during traffic stops in Texas and Maine, officials said. The shift in ⁠arrest tactics, which US President Donald Trump's border czar Tom Homan called a "temporary pause" in vehicle stops, was implemented one day after an ICE agent killed a driver from Colombia in the coastal Maine town of Biddeford, about 24km south of Portland. On 7 July, an ICE officer in Houston fatally shot a man while trying to stop his vehicle. Although both the men shot were characterised by the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), parent agency of ICE, as being "illegal aliens," DHS officials have acknowledged neither was the intended target of deportation operations that led to their deaths.
